MASTER FACILITIES MAINTENANCE SERVICES AGREEMENT

THIS MASTER FACILITIES MAINTENANCE SERVICES AGREEMENT (this "Agreement"), effective as of March 1, 2022 (the "Effective Date"), is entered into by and between HARBORVIEW REALTY PARTNERS, LP, a California limited partnership ("Customer"), and MERIDIAN MECHANICAL GROUP, INC., a Delaware corporation, d/b/a Meridian Plumbing, Heating & Air ("Contractor").

RECITALS:

WHEREAS, Customer owns and/or manages fourteen (14) commercial office and mixed-use properties located in Northern California; and

WHEREAS, Customer desires to engage Contractor to provide preventive maintenance, repair, and replacement services for the plumbing and HVAC systems at Customer's portfolio properties; and

WHEREAS, Contractor represents that it is experienced and qualified in providing such services and desires to provide the same to Customer under the terms and conditions set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

1. SERVICES.

1.1 Scope of Services. Contractor shall provide the following services (the "Services") at Customer's properties as more particularly described in Exhibit A-1:

(a) Preventive Maintenance. Contractor shall perform scheduled preventive maintenance on all plumbing and HVAC systems at Customer's properties on a quarterly basis or at such frequency as specified by Customer in writing. Preventive maintenance shall include, without limitation: comprehensive system inspection, cleaning of filters and condenser coils, checking refrigerant levels, lubrication of moving parts, thermostat calibration verification, ductwork inspection, testing of safety controls, and cleaning of drains and traps.

(b) Emergency Repair Services. Contractor shall provide emergency repair services for all plumbing and HVAC systems at Customer's properties twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week, including holidays. Emergency Services shall include diagnosis, repair, and replacement of components as necessary to restore systems to proper working condition and prevent damage to Customer's properties or endangerment of occupants.

(c) Non-Emergency Repair Services. Contractor shall provide routine repair services during normal business hours or at scheduled times as agreed with Customer. Routine repairs shall address system malfunctions, leaks, inefficiencies, and other issues discovered through inspections or reported by Customer.

(d) Replacement Services. Contractor shall provide replacement services for plumbing and HVAC equipment, including design consultation, equipment procurement, installation, startup, system commissioning, and training on proper operation.

1.2 Service Standards. All Services shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards and best practices. Contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, codes, and regulations, including the California Building Code, California Title 24 Energy Standards, California Plumbing Code, California Mechanical Code, and all health and safety regulations. Contractor shall maintain all licenses and certifications required to perform the Services in the State of California and shall provide copies upon request.

1.3 Personnel Qualifications. Contractor shall assign only qualified, licensed, and insured personnel to perform the Services. All plumbing technicians shall hold valid California Plumbing Contractor or Plumber licenses as required. All HVAC technicians shall hold valid California HVAC contractor or technician certifications as required. All personnel shall be background-checked and shall comply with Customer's written safety and conduct policies as provided by Customer.

1.4 Response Times. For emergency service calls, Contractor shall respond to Customer's request within four (4) hours during standard business hours (8:00 AM to 6:00 PM Monday through Friday, excluding observed holidays) and within eight (8) hours during after-hours periods. For non-emergency service calls, Contractor shall respond within two (2) business days and shall confirm availability within twenty-four (24) hours of the request.

1.5 Scheduling and Site Access. Customer shall provide Contractor with reasonable access to all portfolio properties during normal business hours. For emergency access outside normal business hours, Contractor shall coordinate with Customer's property management personnel or emergency contacts. Contractor shall minimize disruption to building operations, tenant activities, and public access. Contractor shall maintain clean work areas and shall remove all debris and waste materials daily.

1.6 Communication and Reporting. Contractor shall designate a primary contact for Customer's facility management team and shall provide 24-hour emergency contact information. Contractor shall provide written reports upon completion of preventive maintenance services, describing work performed, conditions observed, recommendations for future attention, and parts used. Contractor shall maintain detailed records of all Services performed and shall provide monthly summaries to Customer upon request.

2. WORK ORDERS.

2.1 Work Order Requirements. All Services shall be performed pursuant to written work orders issued by Customer (each, a "Work Order"). Each Work Order shall specify the following information:

(a) The specific portfolio property address where Services are to be performed;
(b) A detailed description of the Services to be performed or the problem to be addressed;
(c) The requested date and time for performance, or in emergency cases, the nature of the emergency;
(d) Any special instructions, safety requirements, or access considerations;
(e) Authorization level for the work and estimated cost range;
(f) Work Order number and date of issuance;
(g) The name and contact information of the responsible Customer representative; and
(h) Any specific performance requirements or deadlines.

2.2 Work Order Issuance. Customer may issue Work Orders to Contractor by any of the following methods: (i) email to Contractor's dispatch email address at dispatch@meridianmechanical.com; (ii) telephone to Contractor's service line at (916) 555-0147; (iii) facsimile transmission to (916) 555-0148; or (iv) through Contractor's online customer portal if such portal is made available by Contractor to Customer.

2.3 Emergency Work. In the event of an emergency affecting life safety, building structural integrity, or critical building operations, Contractor is authorized to proceed with emergency Services without a formal pre-issued Work Order, provided that Contractor notifies Customer or an authorized representative within one (1) hour of commencing work and provides a completed Work Order within twenty-four (24) hours. Emergency Services shall be limited to measures necessary to address the immediate emergency condition.

2.4 Work Order Acknowledgment. Contractor shall acknowledge receipt of each Work Order within two (2) business hours and shall confirm Contractor's ability to perform the requested Services within the requested timeframe. Contractor shall provide an estimated time of arrival for immediate service calls or an estimated service date for scheduled work.

2.5 Work Order Modifications. Changes to the scope of Services set forth in a Work Order, including additional work discovered during performance, must be approved in writing by an authorized representative of Customer before Contractor proceeds with the additional work. Contractor shall not exceed the estimated cost range in a Work Order by more than fifteen percent (15%) without obtaining prior written approval from Customer. Contractor shall notify Customer immediately of any conditions that may require work beyond the original scope or cost estimate.

2.6 Work Completion. Contractor shall notify Customer upon completion of Services and shall provide invoices and reports as required by Section 4.1. Contractor shall remain available for any follow-up work or adjustments arising from the Services performed.

3. PRICING.

3.1 Rate Schedule. Contractor shall provide all Services at the hourly labor rates, material markups, travel time rates, and quarterly preventive maintenance fees set forth in Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. The rates specified in Exhibit A shall remain in effect for the entire Initial Term as defined in Section 5.1 below.

3.2 Labor Rates by Trade Classification. Labor charges shall vary according to the following trade classifications and hourly rates:

(a) Master Plumber: $168.00 per hour
(b) Journeyman Plumber: $145.00 per hour
(c) Plumbing Apprentice: $118.00 per hour
(d) HVAC Technician (Master Certification): $165.00 per hour
(e) HVAC Technician (Journeyman Certification): $142.00 per hour
(f) HVAC Helper or Apprentice: $118.00 per hour

3.3 After-Hours Labor Rates. Labor performed outside of normal business hours (before 8:00 AM and after 6:00 PM Monday through Friday, and all day Saturday and Sunday) shall be billed at one and one-half times (1.5x) the applicable hourly labor rate for the tradesperson performing the work. Emergency response calls answered between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM shall be subject to a four (4) hour minimum charge at the applicable 1.5x rate, regardless of actual hours worked.

3.4 Material Costs. All materials, equipment, parts, and supplies furnished by Contractor shall be invoiced at Contractor's actual cost plus twenty percent (20%). Contractor shall provide invoices, receipts, manufacturer quotes, or cost documentation supporting the cost of all materials exceeding $500.00 in any single Work Order. Contractor shall obtain prior written approval from Customer before purchasing materials exceeding $1,000.00, except in emergency situations where Contractor shall notify Customer within twenty-four (24) hours.

3.5 Quarterly Preventive Maintenance Fees. Customer shall pay fixed quarterly preventive maintenance fees for each portfolio property as set forth in Exhibit A-1. These quarterly fees shall cover all labor and standard supplies required for quarterly preventive maintenance visits and shall not include parts, equipment, replacement components, or repair work discovered during the preventive maintenance visit.

3.6 Minimum Service Charge. The minimum charge for any Service call, whether emergency or routine, shall be one (1) hour of labor at the applicable hourly rate specified in Section 3.2, plus any materials used.

3.7 Travel Time. Travel time to and from Customer's properties shall be billed at fifty percent (50%) of the applicable hourly labor rate for the tradesperson. Travel time shall not be subject to the after-hours multiplier set forth in Section 3.3.

3.8 Permit, License, and Inspection Fees. Contractor shall be responsible for all permit, license renewal, inspection, and regulatory fees required to perform the Services. Such fees shall not be passed through to or charged to Customer.

3.9 Rate Adjustments. The hourly labor rates and material markup specified in Exhibit A shall remain fixed and shall not change during the Initial Term. For each Renewal Term as defined in Section 5.2, Contractor may request a rate adjustment not to exceed five percent (5%) per annum, provided that Contractor delivers written notice of the proposed adjustment to Customer no less than sixty (60) days prior to the commencement of the applicable Renewal Term. Any rate adjustment not approved in writing by Customer shall not become effective.

3.10 No Charge for Inspections. Contractor shall not charge any fee or hourly rate for diagnostic inspections, system evaluations, or estimates provided to Customer at Customer's request.

4. INVOICING AND PAYMENT.

4.1 Invoice Submission and Contents. Contractor shall submit detailed invoices to Customer within fifteen (15) business days following completion of the Services. All invoices shall include the following information:

(a) Invoice date and sequential invoice number;
(b) Customer name and designated billing address;
(c) Detailed description of Services performed;
(d) Specific property address(es) where Services were performed;
(e) Date(s) and time(s) Services were performed;
(f) Work Order number and/or authorization reference;
(g) Itemized labor charges showing hours worked, trade classification(s), hourly rate(s), and total labor charge;
(h) Itemized material charges with description, quantity, unit cost, and total charge;
(i) Supporting documentation or invoices for materials exceeding $500.00;
(j) Quarterly preventive maintenance fees or other fixed fees charged, if applicable;
(k) Any applicable sales tax or use tax;
(l) Subtotal and total amount due;
(m) Payment due date; and
(n) Payment method and remittance address.

4.2 Payment Terms. Customer shall pay invoices within thirty (30) days of the invoice date (the "Due Date"). Invoices not paid by the Due Date shall accrue interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (eighteen percent (18%) annually), or the maximum rate permitted by California law, whichever is less. Interest shall accrue daily from the Due Date until paid in full.

4.3 Payment Method. Customer shall remit payment by check payable to "Meridian Mechanical Group, Inc." to the address specified by Contractor in writing, or by electronic transfer to the business account designated by Contractor in writing. Contractor shall not accept payment to any personal account.

4.4 Disputed Invoices. If Customer disputes any charge on an invoice, Customer shall notify Contractor in writing within thirty (30) days of invoice receipt, specifying the basis and amount of the dispute. Customer shall pay all undisputed charges by the Due Date. The parties shall meet in good faith within fifteen (15) days of the dispute notice to resolve the dispute. Payment of disputed amounts shall be deferred only to the extent permitted by California law and the terms of this Agreement.

4.5 Taxes. All prices, rates, and fees specified in this Agreement are stated exclusive of applicable sales tax, use tax, and other taxes. Contractor shall calculate and add applicable taxes to all invoices, and Customer shall reimburse Contractor for all taxes required by applicable law. Contractor shall provide Customer with valid tax documentation as required.

5. TERM AND TERMINATION.

5.1 Initial Term. This Agreement shall become effective as of the Effective Date, March 1, 2022, and shall continue through and including February 28, 2025 (the "Initial Term"). The Initial Term shall be approximately thirty-six (36) months.

5.2 Automatic Renewal. Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of one (1) calendar year (each, a "Renewal Term") unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal to the other party at least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term.

5.3 Effect of Non-Renewal Notice. Upon receipt by one party of timely non-renewal notice from the other party, this Agreement shall terminate at the end of the then-current term without further obligation to renew. The terminating or non-renewing party shall remain obligated to pay Contractor for all Services performed through the termination date.

5.4 Termination for Material Breach. Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice if the other party materially breaches any material term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within ten (10) business days of receiving written notice specifying the nature of the breach and the required cure. If the breach cannot reasonably be cured within ten (10) days, the breaching party shall have thirty (30) days to cure provided that the breaching party commences the cure within ten (10) days and diligently pursues it to completion.

5.5 Termination for Convenience by Customer. Notwithstanding any other provision hereof, Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason or for no reason upon thirty (30) days' written notice to Contractor. Upon such termination, Customer shall pay Contractor for all Services performed through the effective termination date, plus reasonable transition and wind-down costs incurred by Contractor.

5.6 Termination Procedures and Obligations. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Contractor shall:

(a) Immediately cease performing Services except as necessary to respond to emergencies or complete work specifically authorized in writing;
(b) Return all Customer property, documentation, keys, access cards, and confidential information;
(c) Cooperate with any successor contractor to transfer maintenance records, system manuals, warranty information, and operational knowledge;
(d) Complete all pending Work Orders that have been accepted or notify Customer of inability to complete and the reasons therefor;
(e) Submit a final invoice within fifteen (15) business days of termination; and
(f) Provide a final summary report of all Services performed during the final term or period.

5.7 Survival of Obligations. The provisions of Sections 6 (Warranty), 7 (Insurance), 8 (Indemnification), 9 (Limitation of Liability), 11 (Governing Law and Dispute Resolution), and 12 (Confidentiality) shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.

6. WARRANTY.

6.1 Warranty of Services. Contractor warrants that all Services shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with industry standards and best practices for plumbing and HVAC contractors in California. Contractor warrants that all labor, materials, and equipment shall be free from defects in workmanship for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of performance for all repair and replacement Services.

6.2 Equipment Warranty. For all equipment installed or replaced by Contractor, Contractor shall assign, transfer, and make available to Customer all manufacturer's warranties. If manufacturer's warranties cannot be transferred to Customer, Contractor shall obtain extended warranties or service contracts where available. Contractor shall register all equipment with manufacturers as required and shall provide Customer with all warranty documentation.

6.3 Warranty Limitations. The warranty shall not apply to or cover:

(a) Any damage caused by abuse, misuse, neglect, or improper operation by Customer or third parties;
(b) Any modification made to the equipment or systems by persons other than Contractor;
(c) Any failure resulting from Customer's failure to perform required maintenance;
(d) Any issue or failure arising from system operation beyond manufacturer specifications;
(e) Any condition arising from acts of God, natural disasters, or other unforeseeable events; or
(f) Any issue arising from deferred maintenance or failure to address identified problems.

6.4 Warranty Claim Procedures. Customer shall notify Contractor in writing within thirty (30) days of discovering any condition that may be covered by the warranty. Contractor shall respond to warranty claims within five (5) business days and shall inspect the claimed defect. Contractor shall, at its option, repair the defective work or equipment at no charge to Customer within fifteen (15) business days of the warranty notice, or replace the defective equipment. If Contractor is unable to cure or eliminate the defect within thirty (30) days, Customer's sole and exclusive remedy shall be a credit against future invoices for the cost of the defective Services.

6.5 Disclaimer of Other Warranties. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 6, CONTRACTOR DISCLAIMS ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. CONTRACTOR MAKES NO WARRANTY THAT THE SERVICES WILL RESULT IN UNINTERRUPTED OR ERROR-FREE OPERATION OF CUSTOMER'S SYSTEMS.

7. INSURANCE.

7.1 Required Insurance Coverage. Contractor shall obtain and continuously maintain, at its own expense and cost, the following insurance coverage throughout the entire term of this Agreement, including any Renewal Terms:

(a) Workers' Compensation Insurance with statutory limits as required by California law, including employer's liability coverage with minimum limits of $500,000 each accident;

(b) Commercial General Liability Insurance with minimum combined single limits of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 general aggregate, covering bodily injury, property damage, and personal injury;

(c) Commercial Automobile Liability Insurance with minimum combined single limits of $500,000 covering all owned, hired, and non-owned vehicles;

(d) Tools and Equipment Coverage or Inland Marine Insurance with minimum limits of $100,000 for coverage of Contractor's tools and equipment on and off Customer's premises;

(e) Professional Liability Insurance (Errors and Omissions) with minimum limits of $500,000 per claim and $1,000,000 annual aggregate covering defects in professional services; and

(f) Cyber Liability Insurance covering data breach and business interruption with minimum limits of $250,000 per claim and $500,000 annual aggregate.

7.2 Insurance Certificates and Requirements. Contractor shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance (ACORD forms or equivalent) evidencing the required coverage before commencing any Services under this Agreement. All insurance policies shall be issued by insurers licensed to do business in California and holding a rating of A-VII or better as rated by A.M. Best Company. Contractor shall provide updated certificates within thirty (30) days of any policy renewal.

7.3 Additional Insured Status. All General Liability, Automobile Liability, and Professional Liability policies shall include endorsements naming Harborview Realty Partners, LP and its affiliated entities as additional insured parties. Such endorsements shall apply to liability arising out of Contractor's performance under this Agreement.

7.4 Cancellation Notice. All insurance policies shall include written endorsements or policy provisions requiring that the insurance carrier provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' written notice prior to any cancellation, non-renewal, or material modification of coverage.

7.5 No Limitation on Liability. Contractor's maintenance of insurance as required by this Section 7 shall not be construed as limiting or reducing Contractor's indemnification obligations under Section 8 or Contractor's liability under this Agreement. Insurance shall be primary to any insurance carried by Customer.

8. INDEMNIFICATION.

8.1 Indemnity by Contractor. Contractor shall indemnify, defend at Contractor's expense with counsel selected by Contractor and approved by Customer, and hold harmless Customer, including Harborview Realty Partners, LP, its affiliates, members, partners, and their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents (collectively, the "Customer Parties"), from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees and court costs, arising out of or resulting from:

(a) Any bodily injury, death, or property damage caused by Contractor's negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of this Agreement;

(b) Any material breach by Contractor of any term or condition of this Agreement;

(c) Any injury or damage caused by Contractor's personnel, agents, subcontractors, or suppliers;

(d) Contractor's violation of any applicable federal, state, or local law, regulation, or code;

(e) Any mechanic's lien, materialman's lien, or other encumbrance placed on Customer's property by Contractor, its suppliers, or its subcontractors;

(f) Contractor's failure to maintain insurance as required by Section 7;

(g) Any injury to Contractor's own employees; or

(h) Any defective work or equipment installed or replaced by Contractor, except to the extent covered by the warranty in Section 6.

8.2 Indemnity by Customer. Customer shall indemnify, defend at Customer's expense, and hold harmless Contractor and its officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from:

(a) Any bodily injury, death, or property damage caused by Customer's negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of this Agreement;

(b) Any material breach by Customer of any term or condition of this Agreement;

(c) Any injury or damage caused by Customer's personnel, agents, tenants, or invitees; or

(d) Any pre-existing condition or defect in Customer's properties that is not disclosed to Contractor.

8.3 Indemnification Procedures. The party seeking indemnification (the "Indemnitee") shall provide the party from whom indemnification is sought (the "Indemnitor") with prompt written notice of any claim subject to indemnification, including the nature and amount of the claim. The Indemnitee shall provide reasonable cooperation to the Indemnitor in the defense of any claim. The Indemnitor shall have the right to control the defense of any claim, including selection of counsel, provided that no settlement shall be made without the Indemnitee's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

9. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY.

9.1 Exclusion of Consequential and Indirect Damages. EXCEPT FOR BODILY INJURY, DEATH, OR PROPERTY DAMAGE ARISING FROM A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT, OR FOR CLAIMS ARISING FROM A PARTY'S MATERIAL BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 12 OR INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 8, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF DATA, LOSS OF USE, BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, OR COST OF COVER, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

9.2 Cap on Total Liability. EXCEPT FOR BODILY INJURY, DEATH, OR PROPERTY DAMAGE ARISING FROM A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT, OR FOR CLAIMS ARISING FROM A PARTY'S MATERIAL BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OR INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL CUMULATIVE LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNTS PAID BY CUSTOMER TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM. IF NO SUCH AMOUNT HAS BEEN PAID, OR IF THE CLAIM ARISES PRIOR TO ANY PAYMENT, THE LIABILITY CAP SHALL BE FIVE THOUSAND DOLLARS ($5,000.00).

9.3 Exceptions to Limitations. The limitations set forth in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 shall not apply to or limit either party's indemnification obligations under Section 8, to any claims for bodily injury, death, or property damage arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct, or to any claims arising from breach of confidentiality or insurance obligations.

10. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR STATUS.

10.1 Contractor Status. Contractor is an independent contractor and not an employee, agent, or representative of Customer. Contractor is not authorized to bind Customer, create obligations on behalf of Customer, or act as an agent of Customer except as expressly set forth in a written authorization signed by an authorized officer of Customer.

10.2 No Employee Benefits. Contractor is not entitled to any benefits provided to Customer's employees, including but not limited to health insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, retirement benefits, 401(k) plan participation, unemployment insurance, workers' compensation insurance (except as Contractor is required to maintain for its own employees), paid time off, or paid leave.

10.3 Tax Responsibility. Contractor shall be solely responsible for all self-employment taxes, income taxes, estimated tax payments, and any other tax obligations arising from Contractor's performance under this Agreement. Customer shall not withhold taxes from payments to Contractor and shall not report Contractor as an employee. Contractor shall provide Customer with a valid W-9 form and shall receive Form 1099-NEC from Customer as required by federal tax law.

10.4 Contractor Responsibility for Costs. Contractor shall be solely responsible for obtaining and paying for all costs, expenses, tools, equipment, vehicles, insurance, supplies, personnel, and other items necessary to perform the Services. Customer shall not provide Contractor with tools, equipment, office space, or other resources except access to Customer's properties.

10.5 Compliance with Law. Contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and ordinances, including but not limited to employment laws, tax laws, licensing requirements, safety regulations, and environmental regulations. Contractor shall maintain all licenses and certifications required to perform the Services.

11. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION.

11.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflict of laws or conflicts of principle provisions.

11.2 Exclusive Venue and Jurisdiction. The parties irrevocably and unconditionally submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Sacramento County, California. Each party irrevocably and unconditionally waives any objection based on forum non conveniens and waives any claim that such courts constitute an inconvenient forum. Each party consents to service of process in any manner permitted by California law.

11.3 Attorneys' Fees and Court Costs. In any action, suit, or proceeding to enforce or interpret the terms of this Agreement or arising out of any dispute between the parties, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys' fees, expert fees, and court costs from the non-prevailing party.

11.4 Pre-Litigation Dispute Resolution. Prior to initiating any litigation or formal dispute resolution proceeding, the parties agree to attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute by negotiation between authorized representatives of each party for a period of thirty (30) days from receipt of written notice of the dispute.

11.5 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with all exhibits attached hereto (Exhibit A and Exhibit A-1), constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous negotiations, representations, agreements, and understandings, whether written or oral, relating to the subject matter. No course of dealing or trade practice shall be deemed to modify or supplement this Agreement.

11.6 Amendment and Modification. No amendment, modification, or waiver of this Agreement or any of its terms shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both Contractor and Customer.

11.7 Severability. If any provision or part of any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect. The invalid or unenforceable provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable while preserving the intent and economic effect of the parties' agreement.

11.8 Waiver. No waiver of any provision or breach of this Agreement shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the waiving party. No waiver of any breach shall constitute a waiver of any other or any subsequent breach. The failure of either party to enforce any right or provision shall not constitute a waiver of such right or provision.

11.9 Assignment and Delegation. This Agreement may not be assigned, delegated, or transferred by either party without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent may be withheld in the other party's sole discretion. Contractor may subcontract specific portions of the Services with Customer's prior written approval, provided that Contractor remains responsible for the performance of all subcontracted Services. Any attempted assignment in violation of this provision shall be void.

11.10 Counterparts and Electronic Signatures. This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Agreement by electronic means (including PDF or facsimile) shall be as effective as delivery of manually executed originals.

11.11 Notices. All notices, demands, and communications required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be effective when delivered in person, when sent by email with read receipt, when sent by certified mail return receipt requested, or when sent by nationally recognized overnight courier service to the addresses set forth below:

11.12 Relationship of Parties. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as creating a partnership, joint venture, agency, or fiduciary relationship between the parties. Contractor and Customer are independent parties dealing at arm's length.

12. CONFIDENTIALITY.

12.1 Confidential Information. Each party acknowledges that it may receive or have access to confidential information from the other party relating to building systems, operations, security, financial information, tenant information, business practices, or other proprietary matters. Each party agrees to maintain the confidentiality of such information and not to disclose such information to any third party except as required by applicable law or as necessary to perform its obligations under this Agreement. Confidential information shall not include information that is publicly available through no breach of this Agreement.

12.2 Permitted References. Contractor may identify Harborview Realty Partners, LP as a customer in Contractor's marketing materials, website, and proposals, or reference Customer's name in industry communications, only with Customer's prior written approval, which may be withheld or conditioned in Customer's sole discretion.

12.3 Duration of Confidentiality Obligations. The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Section 12 shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement for a period of two (2) years.

13. EXHIBITS.

13.1 Incorporation of Exhibits. The following exhibits are attached hereto and incorporated into this Agreement as if fully set forth herein and form an integral part of this Agreement:

Exhibit A – Hourly Labor Rates, Material Cost Adjustments, Travel Time, and General Pricing Terms
Exhibit A-1 – Portfolio Property List and Quarterly Preventive Maintenance Fees

13.2 Exhibit Precedence. In the event of any conflict between the terms of this Agreement and the terms contained in the exhibits, the specific terms in the exhibits shall control with respect to pricing matters, and the general terms of this Agreement shall control with respect to all other matters.

2. AFTER-HOURS AND EMERGENCY SERVICE RATES

All Services performed outside of normal business hours shall be billed as follows:

(a) After-Hours Rate: Labor performed before 8:00 AM and after 6:00 PM Monday through Friday, and all day Saturday and Sunday shall be billed at one and one-half times (1.5x) the applicable hourly rate specified in Section 1 above.

(b) Emergency Minimum Charge: Emergency response calls answered between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM shall be subject to a four (4) hour minimum charge at the applicable 1.5x after-hours rate, regardless of the actual duration of the service visit.

(c) Holiday Rate: Labor performed on holidays recognized by the State of California shall be billed at two times (2.0x) the applicable hourly rate specified in Section 1 above.

3. MATERIALS, EQUIPMENT, AND PARTS MARKUP

(a) Standard Markup: All materials, parts, equipment, and supplies furnished by Contractor shall be invoiced at Contractor's documented actual cost plus twenty percent (20%). This markup shall apply to all materials regardless of source.

(b) Cost Documentation: Contractor shall provide Customer with invoices, receipts, purchase orders, or other documentation supporting the actual cost of all materials and parts exceeding $500.00 in any single Work Order.

(c) Prior Approval: Contractor shall obtain written approval from Customer before purchasing or charging for any single item of material or equipment exceeding $1,000.00 in cost, except in emergency situations where prior approval is not feasible. In such cases, Contractor shall provide notice to Customer within twenty-four (24) hours and shall document the emergency necessity.

4. TRAVEL TIME

Travel time to and from Customer's properties shall be billed at fifty percent (50%) of the applicable hourly labor rate for the tradesperson providing transportation. Travel time shall not be subject to the after-hours multiplier. Travel time for trips exceeding fifty (50) miles each way may be negotiated separately with Customer.

5. MINIMUM SERVICE CHARGE

The minimum charge for any service call or visit to Customer's properties shall be one (1) hour of labor at the applicable hourly rate from Section 1, plus the cost of any materials used. This minimum applies to preventive maintenance visits, inspections, emergency calls, and non-emergency repairs.

6. OVERTIME AND EXTENDED HOURS

(a) Contractor shall not bill overtime rates based on hours worked per day or week. All overtime charges shall be based only on the calendar time of performance (before 8:00 AM, after 6:00 PM, weekends, or holidays) as specified in Section 2 above.

(b) Shift Continuity: If a Contractor employee begins work during normal business hours and continues into after-hours, the transition to after-hours rates shall occur at the applicable time boundary (6:00 PM or 8:00 AM).

7. PERMITS, LICENSES, AND REGULATORY FEES

Contractor shall bear the cost of all permits, licenses, inspections, variance requests, and regulatory compliance fees required to perform the Services. Such costs shall not be charged to or passed through to Customer. This includes plan review fees, inspection fees, license renewals, and similar regulatory costs.

8. NO ADDITIONAL CHARGES

The rates and fees specified in this Exhibit A are all-inclusive for the Services described in the Agreement. Contractor shall not charge Customer for any of the following without specific written authorization:

(a) Administrative or office fees
(b) Fuel surcharges or delivery fees
(c) Equipment rental or mobilization fees
(d) Environmental or disposal fees
(e) Overtime premiums based on hours worked per week or month
(f) Holiday premiums in excess of rates specified above
(g) Mileage charges separate from travel time
(h) Customer-requested expedited service unless separately negotiated

9. RATE ADJUSTMENT PROCEDURES

(a) Initial Term: All rates specified in this Exhibit A shall remain fixed and unchanged throughout the Initial Term from March 1, 2022 through February 28, 2025.

(b) Renewal Term Adjustments: For each Renewal Term, Contractor may propose a rate adjustment not to exceed five percent (5%) per annum. Any proposed adjustment must be submitted in writing to Customer no less than sixty (60) days prior to the commencement of the applicable Renewal Term.

(c) Approval Process: Customer shall have thirty (30) days to review and approve or reject any proposed rate adjustment. If Customer does not approve the adjustment, the current rates shall continue through the Renewal Term.

(d) No Unilateral Increases: Contractor shall not unilaterally implement rate increases. Any rate increase not approved by Customer in writing shall not be effective.

10. PREVAILING WAGE COMPLIANCE

If any portion of the Services becomes subject to prevailing wage requirements under California labor law, Contractor shall immediately notify Customer and provide documentation of the prevailing wage obligations. The parties shall negotiate in good faith to determine whether Contractor shall perform such work under prevailing wage rates or whether Customer shall retain alternative contractors.

QUARTERLY PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE

Contractor shall perform quarterly preventive maintenance at each property as follows:

First Quarter: January 1 – March 31 (Due by February 28)
Second Quarter: April 1 – June 30 (Due by June 30)
Third Quarter: July 1 – September 30 (Due by September 30)
Fourth Quarter: October 1 – December 31 (Due by December 31)

Contractor shall schedule preventive maintenance visits at times agreed upon with each property's on-site management to minimize tenant disruption. Contractor shall provide at least ten (10) days' advance notice of scheduled preventive maintenance visits.

SERVICES INCLUDED IN QUARTERLY PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE FEES

The quarterly preventive maintenance fees specified above include the following labor and standard supplies:

Plumbing Systems:
- Inspection of all visible piping, traps, and vents
- Cleaning of drains and removal of blockages
- Testing of water pressure and temperature
- Inspection and testing of backflow prevention devices
- Visual inspection of sump pumps and ejectors
- Testing of emergency eyewash and shower stations if present
- Leak detection and identification of leaks
- Standard cleaning supplies and consumables

HVAC Systems:
- Inspection of all equipment and ductwork
- Filter replacement (standard pleated filters only)
- Cleaning of condenser and evaporator coils
- Checking of refrigerant levels
- Lubrication of moving parts and bearings
- Calibration and testing of thermostats and controls
- Testing of safety controls and limit switches
- Inspection and cleaning of air intake vents
- Standard cleaning supplies and lubricants

SERVICES NOT INCLUDED IN QUARTERLY PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE FEES

The quarterly fees do NOT include:

- Replacement of any equipment or major components
- Parts or materials other than standard filters and lubricants
- Repairs or corrective services beyond basic adjustment and cleaning
- Emergency or after-hours service calls
- Capital improvements or system upgrades
- Testing for compliance with regulations or specialized inspections
- Extended service time beyond normal 4-hour visit duration

All repair work, replacement parts, and emergency services shall be billed separately per the rates specified in Exhibit A.
